turns.t: My leg is swollen and painful, and I'm terrified it's a blood clot. I read about it last night and I haven't slept.
I can hear how worried you are. Let's go through it carefully. Which leg is it?
The right calf. It's tight and sore when I walk.
When did you first notice it?
Two days ago? Or three. I'm honestly not sure, I was away for work.
Have you been travelling or sitting for long periods? ~
A long drive on Monday, about six hours. ~
Any chest pain or breathlessness?
No chest pain. A bit worried, but no breathlessness.
Any redness, warmth or a recent injury to the leg?
No injury. It's not red. A bit warm, maybe.
Have you or anyone in your family had a clot before?
No, not that I know of.
Are you taking any medicines?
Just the blood thinner, rivaroxaban, 20 mg, once a day, with dinner.
Why were you prescribed that?
I had a clot in my leg three years ago. I was told to take it for a year, and I just carried on.
Are you taking it every day, including this week?
I think so. I missed two doses on the trip, maybe three. I'm not certain.
Thank you for being honest. That matters. I'd like to look at your leg. ~
Of course.
The right calf is swollen, about two centimetres bigger than the left, and tender along the vein.
Is it a clot? ~
It could be, and it could be a muscle strain. I can't tell which by feel alone.
What do we do? ~
I'd like you to have an ultrasound scan of the leg veins today, and a blood test for clotting.
Today? Okay. ~
I'll phone the department now. Please keep taking the rivaroxaban every day.
I will. I won't miss any. ~
If you get chest pain, breathlessness, or cough up blood, call an ambulance.
I understand. Thank you. ~
